title: Slips, trips and falls
siteNotes: Where wet floor signs, mops, spill kits and cleaning equipment are kept
Which footwear the venue expects for each department
Who to report a hazard to on each shift (and the venue's hazard reporting method)
Known problem areas such as cellar steps, kitchen floors, the marquee and outdoor paths in winter
legalNotes: Employers must ensure staff health and safety so far as reasonably practicable, and staff must take reasonable care and co-operate: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, ss. 2 and 7. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1974/37
Training on induction and when risks change: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, reg. 13. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/1999/3242

Slips and trips are prevented by understanding causes and acting on contamination, cleaning, footwear, obstructions, lighting and reporting: HSE, https://www.hse.gov.uk/slips/ (the overview page was checked; the detailed 'causes' pages could not be loaded in this session).

Clean up spills straight away, use warning signs while a floor is wet, and keep floors dry and clear: standard HSE advice for hospitality; consistent with the HSE overview but not tied to a specific page here.
Reporting: staff report hazards and accidents; the accident book and RIDDOR are covered in the first-aid-accidents session.
No statistics are quoted. The index blurb says slips are the biggest cause of injury in hospitality; that claim was not verified in this session, so the slides do not repeat it as a figure.

Review Oct 2026: s.2/s.7 HSWA 1974 and reg. 13 MHSWR 1999 confirmed. Check 16 option A changed: 'keep to the handrail side' was not clearly wrong, because carrying a load you cannot see over is the hazard whichever side you walk. The marked answer (split the load or ask for help) is unchanged.

cards.title: Slips, trips and falls
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- spot the common causes in your work area
- deal with a hazard straight away
- report what you cannot fix yourself

cards.title: A fall can happen to anyone
cards.body:
Wet floors, cables, boxes and steps are part of working in a hotel, bar, kitchen or marquee. A fall can hurt a colleague or a guest, and often takes only a moment. Most can be prevented by small habits.

> If you see it, you own it, either by fixing it or by reporting it.

items.title: Slips
items.text: Spills, wet floors, grease and ice.

items.title: Trips
items.text: Cables, boxes, mats and uneven ground.

items.title: Falls
items.text: Stairs, steps and reaching for high shelves.

cards.title: Where it happens here
cards.body: Know where the risks are in your area, then check them as you work.

items.title: Bar and cellar
items.text: Spilled drinks, hoses and cellar steps.

items.title: Marquee and outdoors
items.text: Wires, matting, wet grass and ice.

cards.title: Spills: deal with it straight away
cards.body: A spill is a hazard the moment it lands. Stay with it or mark it, and do not walk past.

items.title: Warn
items.text: Put a wet floor sign out.

items.title: Clean
items.text: Mop or wipe it up, or get the right kit.

items.title: Dry
items.text: Check the floor is dry before removing the sign.

items.title: Report
items.text: If you cannot fix it, tell your manager.

cards.title: Floors, stairs and cables
cards.body:
Keep walkways clear of boxes, bins, trolleys and bags. Tell your manager if a light is out or a carpet or mat is lifting. Cables should be routed away from where people walk, or covered with a proper cover.

- Use handrails on stairs
- Do not carry so much you cannot see your feet

cards.title: Use the right steps
cards.body:
Never stand on a chair, a barrel or a crate to reach something high. Use the steps or kick stool provided, on a flat floor, and ask for help if there is nothing suitable.

> Your manager will show you where the steps are kept.

items.title: Ask for help
items.text: If steps are not available or you feel unsafe.

items.title: Avoid reaching
items.text: Store heavy or often-used items low.

cards.title: Shoes make a difference
cards.body:
Wear shoes that are in good condition, fit well and suit your job. A worn sole on a wet kitchen or bar floor is a risk to you.

> Your manager will tell you what footwear your department expects.

cards.title: Report it, even if nobody fell
cards.body: If you cannot put a hazard right yourself, tell your manager and warn others in the meantime. If someone falls, even if they say they are fine, tell your manager so it can be recorded.

items.title: Make safe
items.text: Warn others or block the area.

items.title: Record
items.text: Any fall or near miss gets written down.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- If you see a hazard, deal with it or report it
- Clean up spills straight away, and use a sign
- Keep floors, stairs and exits clear
- Use proper steps, never a chair
- Wear suitable footwear and report any fall

cards.q: You spot a puddle of lager by the bar and you are carrying two plates. What do you do?
options: Step round it carefully and tell someone later
Wait for the cleaner to find it on their round
Put the plates down safely, then warn and clear it
Put a bar towel over it so it is not seen
cards.why: Hazards are dealt with straight away. Warn others, clear the spill, and check the floor is dry. Walking past leaves it for someone else to fall on.

cards.q: It is fine to stand on a sturdy chair to reach a high shelf for a moment.
cards.why: Chairs are not designed for standing on. Use proper steps or ask for help.

cards.q: A cable for the DJ runs across the marquee walkway. What is the best action?
options: Tell the DJ and your manager so it can be moved or covered
Leave it where it is, as guests can see it
Tape a napkin over it so it is more visible
Move it yourself and say nothing to anyone
cards.why: Cables across walkways are trip hazards. Report so it can be rerouted or properly covered.

cards.q: Which TWO are good habits for preventing falls?
options: Carrying so much you cannot see the floor
Using handrails on stairs
Leaving boxes in the corridor for a minute
Reporting a lamp that is out
Wearing worn smooth soles
cards.why: Handrails and reporting lighting faults help prevent falls. The others create hazards.

cards.q: A colleague slips on a wet floor, says 'I'm fine' and carries on. What should happen?
options: Nothing, as they said they are fine and carried on
Only report it if they end up going to hospital
Wait to see if they are sore the next day
Report it to the manager so it is recorded
cards.why: Falls are reported even when nobody seems hurt. It protects the person if pain shows later, and helps fix the cause.

cards.q: If a floor is wet because it has just been mopped, a wet floor sign can be left out all day to be safe.
cards.why: Signs warn while the floor is wet. Check it is dry, then remove the sign so it does not become ignored.

cards.q: A guest's suitcase is in the corridor outside a room, and you need to pass with a trolley. What is the safest choice?
options: Squeeze past quickly while it is quiet
Ask the guest to move it, or tell the manager
Push the case aside with the front of the trolley
Leave the trolley behind it and come back later
cards.why: Walkways need to stay clear. Ask for it to be moved or report it rather than risk a trip.

cards.q: You are carrying a stack of boxes and cannot see over them. The stairs are ahead. What do you do?
options: Take it slowly, feeling for each step with your foot
Lean the stack on your chest
Go quickly before anyone is on the stairs
Split it into smaller loads or ask for help
cards.why: Do not carry so much that you cannot see where you are going. Use handrails and take smaller loads.

cards.q: Wearing shoes with smooth worn soles on a wet kitchen floor does not matter, as long as you are careful.
cards.why: Worn soles lose grip. Suitable footwear in good condition is part of preventing slips.

cards.q: You notice a bulb has gone in a back stairwell. What should you do?
options: Use the torch on your phone and say nothing
Wait for the next health and safety check
Tell your manager so it can be fixed
Close the door to it
cards.why: Poor lighting is a hazard. Report it, and warn others until it is fixed.
